name: Southern New Jersey Steel Co
old_description: The multifaceted capabilities of Southern New Jersey Steel enable us to provide an array of services to meet the most diverse project requirements.
about:
Southern New Jersey Steel (SNJS) operates from Vineland, New Jersey, tracing its roots to 1975. The company began as a steel contracting firm serving the construction industry across the Eastern United States.

SNJS provides structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication and erection services. Its partnering facilities hold American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) certification and run CNC drill lines, CNC angle lines, and computerized plate burning equipment for oxygen and plasma cutting. The shop produces bolted shop connections, clips, lintels, one-piece trusses, and a range of miscellaneous items including stairs, rails, ladders, grating, spiral stairs, monumental stairs, glass railings, and bronze railings. Pipe rails are formed on a mandrel bending machine to eliminate extra components. The company also supplies steel joists and metal decking, manages erection through experienced subcontractors, and uses Tekla Structures for 3D drafting, BIM modeling, and engineering calculations.

The contractor works directly with public entities and general contractors on projects valued from hundreds to several million dollars. Its portfolio spans public construction such as schools, libraries, prisons, and municipal buildings; industrial work at refineries and manufacturing plants; private commercial projects including supermarkets, retail centers, and warehouses; medical facilities such as Shore Memorial Hospital and Kennedy Health; and higher education projects at Rowan University and the University of Pennsylvania. SNJS is also licensed for casino construction in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

The company emphasizes performance and precision, aiming to deliver maximum customer satisfaction regardless of project complexity or timeline. It maintains bonding resources that meet mandatory criteria and holds approved-contractor status in multiple states for public works.

Leadership is headed by CEO Cara Colgin Smith, who directs a team of territory managers covering distinct geographic zones.

The firm does not manufacture products but provides a suite of field services that support the specification and adoption of rehabilitation technology. Its representatives supply free trial demonstration equipment for therapist and dealer evaluations, conduct in-service training on new rehab devices, and furnish current ordering information, clinical-study data, and sample medical-justification documentation. They also customize equipment configurations for individual patients and consult with rehabilitation clinics on cost-effective product selection.

Primary customers are rehabilitation facilities, clinics, dealers, and therapy professionals who require high-end mobility and positioning solutions. The company focuses on high-end rehabilitation manufacturers and distributors, bringing customized mobility solutions to providers, therapists, and facilities. Examples include physical therapists, occupational therapists, and rehab clinics across the Southwest.

The company distinguishes itself by acting as a consultant to rehabilitation clinics to determine the most cost-effective products and supplies, and by educating the market on the latest rehab technology. Their goal is to ensure the most appropriate equipment reaches the end user.

name: Southwestern Wire
old_description: Some of the website features are unavailable unless JavaScript is enabled.
about:
Southwestern Wire is headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, and traces its origins to March 1992 when Max Moore and Steve Peters acquired the machinery and equipment of Acme Fence and Iron from the Bank of Oklahoma. The founders spent the first year rebuilding and modernizing the plant, installing a state‑of‑the‑art wire galvanizing line that enabled heavier zinc coatings up to 1.2 oz./sq. ft. and positioned the company to compete with larger domestic and foreign wire manufacturers.

The company manufactures a broad range of wire and fence products: galvanized and vinyl‑coated chain link fence fabric (including preslatted and security mini‑mesh up to 20 ft tall), fabricated panel products such as residential bent‑frame gates, dog kennels and temporary fence panels, agricultural wire (vineyard, trellis, high‑tensile and electric fence wire), industrial low‑ and high‑carbon wire (C1006–C1026 and 1027–1065), recycling wire (single‑loop bale ties in black annealed and galvanized finishes), and galvanized tension bars, truss rods, drop rods and gate rods. Southwestern Wire owns and operates three manufacturing facilities in the United States — Norman, OK; Birmingham, AL; and Sacramento, CA — with a major 30,000 sq. ft. expansion added in 1998.

Primary customers are expert distributors in each product category. The company serves the chain link fence industry, industrial wire users, recycling and baling operations, high‑carbon wire markets, agricultural sectors (vineyards, cattle grazing), and security/prison construction where its mini‑mesh products are specified.

Southwestern Wire emphasizes domestic production — "products melted and manufactured in the United States of America" — and points to its 1993 establishment of the only mass‑production galvanized tension bar facility in the U.S. as a key differentiator. The ability to apply Class 5 galvanizing (2 oz./sq. ft.) meeting ASTM A392 Class 2, along with ongoing investments in technology and employee development, underpins its "Made In The USA" positioning.

name: Specialty Food Process Technologies, LLC
old_description: Clean-In-Place systems ensure consistent and repeatable cleaning of process equipment.
about:
Specialty Food Process Technologies, LLC is a process engineering and consulting firm based in Madison, Wisconsin. The company focuses exclusively on food and beverage processing, drawing on an engineering team with a combined 100 years of hands-on experience in the design, construction, and commissioning of turnkey processing plants.

The firm provides a range of engineering services, from early conceptual designs to detailed engineering packages. Core capabilities include Clean-In-Place (CIP) system design, liquid processing systems for blending and dosing liquids, slurries, gases, and powders, and thermal processing systems with automated temperature control and energy recovery. The company also conducts feasibility studies for plant revamps, develops life-cycle roadmaps for existing facilities, and designs aseptic processing and process control systems. A warehouse on site supports spare parts packing and shipping.

Specialty Food Process Technologies serves a broad spectrum of food and beverage sectors. Its project experience spans fluid milk processing, plant oil extraction, grape and orange juice production, tomato processing, milk powder, carbonated beverages, extended shelf-life products, packaged salads, sauces, fried foods, meat processing (ground beef, sausage), baking mixes, prepared meals, baker's yeast, grain handling, infant formula, sugar syrups, powdered ingredients, flavors, pet food, water, coffee, tea, plant-based proteins, and utility systems such as clean steam, compressed air, cooling towers, and glycol chillers. A recent engagement included engineering services and processing equipment for three greenfield fruit and vegetable plants for Pacific Concentrates.

The company emphasizes its hands-on experience as a differentiator, using it to help clients evaluate existing equipment, optimize asset use through life-cycle roadmaps, and solve unique processing problems. It positions itself as a partner for new facility projects and for revamping aging plants.

name: Specialty Foods
old_description: We're a family-owned, family-operated food company located in the heart of Middle Tennessee.
about:
Specialty Foods is a family-owned and family-operated food manufacturer based in La Vergne, Tennessee, in the heart of Middle Tennessee. The company was founded in 2009 by Randall "Randy" Sanders, who identified a gap in the bread market for a top-quality product baked with fine ingredients that delivered a genuine homemade taste. Sanders was later joined by his two sons, Wesley and Will, and together they built the business around three distinct brand lines.

The company produces three product families: Ma's Kitchen, which began in 1985 with a sourdough bread recipe passed down for over a century and initially supplied to restaurant chains; Ginny's Homemade Waffles, made with an age-old recipe that includes imported pearl sugar; and Mama Turney's Homemade Pies. Specialty Foods serves both the food-service channel and the consumer marketplace, emphasizing the use of the freshest ingredients and consistent quality across every batch.

Its customers include restaurant chains, food-service distributors, and retail consumers seeking wholesale or direct purchase options. The company highlights its wholesale resources and food-service resources as part of its offering, targeting operators who value consistent, made-from-scratch baked goods.

Sanders started Specialty Foods to deliver the true look, feel, and taste of homemade baking at a commercial scale, and the company states that its commitment to quality and consistency—every bite, every time—sets it apart from competitors.

about:
Stout's Metal Products operates from Collingswood, New Jersey, where it was officially established in 1985 by Larry Stout and his wife Julianne. The business traces its roots to the 1960s when Larry's father, Ken Stout, a former Navy Yard shipbuilder, opened an ornamental metal shop in Atco. In 1984 the couple purchased a 300‑year‑old property with a rear workspace that had served as an 1880s ice house, a trailer storage shed, and a chicken coop, converting it into their fabrication shop.

The company provides custom metal fabrication and welding services, producing railings and balcony systems (steel, aluminum, wrought iron), ornamental and security fences and gates, ADA‑compliant safety railings, window security bars, and custom metal furniture, truck racks, dock ramps, Bilco doors, and artistic metalwork. They also offer on‑site and mobile welding for structural steel modification, equipment repair, and emergency fixes. The shop serves residential, commercial, and trade clients across South Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania, and the Jersey Shore, with over 8,000 projects completed.

Customers include homeowners, contractors, business owners, and property managers. Notable projects include railings for the Scottish Rite Auditorium, steel piping for the Battleship New Jersey dock in Camden, and a custom iron gate for former Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter. The firm's work has been featured in the local Courier Post newspaper.

The Stouts emphasize understanding each client's needs, maintaining clear communication and schedules, and delivering work to the highest standard every time. They describe their motivation as carrying on a family passion, preserving the art of ornamental metalwork, and creating quality pieces that last for generations.

Sturges Electronics LLC was founded in 1978 in Dryden, New York, as a woman-owned small business specializing in custom wire and cable harness assemblies. The company has operated continuously from its upstate New York location for over four decades.

The company provides custom "build to print" wire and cable harnesses ranging from simple two-circuit assemblies to complex designs with 50 or more circuits, using wire gauges from 30 AWG to 2 AWG. Sturges serves the industrial, defense, medical, transportation, and military markets, delivering harnesses for applications in those sectors.

Sturges differentiates itself through its ISO 9001:2015 certification, IPC/WHMA-A-620 specialist certified inspectors, ITAR registration, and cybersecurity compliance, all within a woman-owned small business structure that emphasizes responsive service for both prototype and high-volume orders.

about:
Summers Manufacturing, Inc. is based in Devils Lake, North Dakota. The company traces its roots to 1965 when Harley Summers purchased patent rights for Goebel truck and pickup hoists and began production in a small shop in Maddock, ND. He incorporated the business as Summers Manufacturing Company, Inc. in 1969. In 2007, the company became 100 percent employee-owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP).

The company designs and manufactures a range of agricultural equipment, including tillage tools (vertical tillage, variable-rate tillage, disk rippers, chisel plows, harrows, and rolling choppers), land rollers (coil packers, hydraulic-fold and trail-type Super Rollers), application equipment (Spray Fill Xpress sprayer fill systems, grain handling conveyors, and field belts), mounted attachments (harrows, rolling baskets, rolling choppers), and rock pickers. Production takes place at its Devils Lake campus, which includes a 26,000-square-foot factory built in 1980 and expanded multiple times through 2010, and an Aberdeen, South Dakota facility added in 2013 for assembly, parts, and distribution.

The company collaborates with research and technology partners such as Grand Farm (Fargo, ND), AgRevival (Gibbon, MN), PTI (Pontiac, IL), and Mach to develop variable-rate tillage and precision agriculture solutions.

The company emphasizes field-tested durability, citing its 2000 introduction of the industry's first true vertical tillage tool (the Supercoulter) and a 10-year limited warranty on select land roller models launched in 2018. Its stated mission is to build field-tested tough equipment that helps farmers feed and fuel the world.

name: Supercar System
about:
Supercar System operates from a factory at 5345 E North Belt Road in North Las Vegas, Nevada. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are the names of its founders.

The company designs and builds F1-style six-speed sequential transmissions rated for up to 1,200 horsepower and 1,000 lb-ft of torque, with shift times quoted at 20 milliseconds. The units use 25 mm helical-cut gears that are case-hardened, precision-ground, and cryogenically treated, housed in a transverse stack for mass centralization. A limited-slip differential, integrated oil pump, and compatibility with GM LS and LT V8 blocks (via optional bolt-on bellhousing) round out the transmission package. Supercar System also lists "turnkey supercars and components" among its product offerings.

The transmissions target builders of high-performance street and track vehicles using GM V8 platforms, as well as integrators developing complete supercar programs. The quick-change rear-end ratios (3.75:1 ring and pinion) and multiple-orientation mounting suit both highway and circuit applications.

The company emphasizes gear strength, noise reduction, and compact packaging as core design goals, citing military-grade heat treatment and open-faced female dog rings for rapid shift response. No explicit founding mission or differentiator statement beyond the technical specifications is provided.

about:
Surf-Tech Manufacturing Corporation was founded in 1989 in Ronkonkoma, New York, in the technology and industry-rich heart of Suffolk County on Long Island. The company began as a contract manufacturer serving a broad range of industries and has remained at the same location, which offers quick access to component suppliers and transportation infrastructure, including proximity to Long Island MacArthur Airport.

The company provides full-service electronic manufacturing and assembly, specializing in surface mount technology (SMT), through-hole (TH) assembly, electro-mechanical box-build, and BGA assembly, rework, and replacement. Services extend from prototype design to end-customer webstore fulfillment.

Surf-Tech serves customers across diverse industries, though the company does not publicly list specific sectors. The company emphasizes quality and lean manufacturing, holding ISO 9001:2015 certification continuously since 2012 with zero third-party audit nonconformances. All inspectors maintain IPC-A-610 certification, and the facility uses a Cyberoptics 3D SQL automated inspection system for solder joint review and a VJ Electronicx X-ray machine for BGA and QFN inspection. Returns are reported at less than 0.01% annually, and functional testing is performed to customer-supplied fixtures and procedures.

about:
TREIF USA Inc, with its website at marel.com, is headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut. The company operates as JBT Marel, a global leader in advanced automation for the food and beverage industry.

JBT Marel designs and delivers a comprehensive portfolio that spans high-performing standalone machines to fully integrated, end-to-end processing lines. Its equipment solutions cover primary processing, further processing, refrigeration, and end-of-line packaging across protein, produce, and plant-based categories. Complementing the hardware, the company provides purpose-built food processing software that integrates machine, process, and business data to enable real-time insights, traceability compliance, and preventative maintenance. A global service network — 133 locations across 29 countries — offers lifetime support through service agreements, spare parts, and on-site expertise, anchored by Customer Technology Centers such as the Lakeland Customer Innovation Center where processors can trial technologies like the Flip & Wash bin washer.

The company serves a broad spectrum of food and beverage sectors, including poultry, meat, fish and seafood, prepared foods, ready meals, beverages and juices, fruit and vegetables, plant-based products, dairy and cheese, pet food, material handling automation, pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals, and water treatment. Notable references include the adoption of Townsend skinners as a standard in the U.S. meat industry and a long-standing partnership with Marlow Foods for plant-based production.

JBT Marel positions its differentiation on the seamless integration of equipment, software, and lifetime service to help customers produce the most value from the least resources. Its automation strategy addresses labor shortages while improving food safety, and its sustainability focus targets energy and water savings, waste reduction, and better raw-material utilization. The firm emphasizes co-creation with customers through its regional technology centers to develop tailored solutions.

about:
TZ Medical Inc was founded in 1990 by Tom Tribou in a Portland, Oregon coffee shop. Now headquartered in Tualatin, Oregon, the company began with a two-part philosophy: listen to front-line medical professionals to understand their needs before engineering solutions, and price those solutions at a value level so they reach critical-care providers faster.

Its portfolio includes radial access sheaths such as the Skyline XT™ thin-wall sheath, the Cobra Board radial buttress device, radiation protection systems under the URPro line, cardiac monitoring solutions, the Beata Clasp® medical line organizer, the Pullie™ surgical pannus retractor, anesthesia tube holders, and lead apron racks. Products are sold across the United States and internationally.

TZ Medical serves hospitals, catheterization labs, labor and delivery units, and cardiac monitoring programs. Customers cited in company materials include Abington Jefferson Health, O'Connor Hospital, Providence Newberg Medical Center, The Christ Hospital, and Presence St. Joseph Medical Center in Joliet.

The founding premise remains the company's stated differentiator: ideas originate from clinicians, not internal engineers alone, and pricing is structured to be accessible without tiered purchasing commitments. The company also emphasizes responsive customer service and tailored account support.

The company emphasizes its identity as “Genuine Saab People” who use the parts they sell, highlighting knowledgeable, prompt, and enthusiastic service. Its in-house manufacturing and dyno capabilities allow for product validation and custom parts development, differentiating it from pure resellers.

The company emphasizes on-time, on-budget performance and an integrated "simulation to prototype to production" model that combines design, machining, electronics, and inspection in a single facility.

name: Tezzaron Semiconductor Corporation
old_description: TSV-free 3D: Stacks the size of a single die. Better by design.
about:
Tezzaron Semiconductor Corporation is headquartered in Naperville, Illinois. The company entered the spotlight in 2004 when it demonstrated the world's first successful wafer-stacked 3D integrated circuits with through-silicon interconnects, including microprocessors, sensors, and SRAM devices. While the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the firm has since collaborated with dozens of customers to develop custom 3D-ICs for both prototyping and commercial production.

Tezzaron's core offering is its Di3D technology, a transistor-level 3D integration platform that combines wafer bonding, proprietary SuperContacts®, dis-integrated architectures, and BiSTAR® programmable self-test. The company handles the full development flow: adapting design tools, rewriting floor-planning rules, inventing and fabricating new structures, and creating novel test techniques and circuits. This end-to-end capability enables high-density, high-speed vertical interconnects in a footprint the size of a single die.

The technology targets high-performance semiconductor applications, including microprocessors, sensors, and memory devices. Tezzaron has participated in multiple multi-project wafer (MPW) runs for 3D-IC prototypes, partnering with organizations such as CMP (Circuits Multi Projets) in France. Its customer base spans companies seeking custom 3D-IC solutions for prototyping and volume commercialization.

The company states that its approach "changes everything" about 3D integration, aiming to build a Di3D™ ecosystem of partners and licensees where the high-performance world can raise the bar for density and speed.

about:
The business launched in June 2012 when chef Mark LaCasse and his wife Kelly returned to central Maine after years of culinary and hospitality work across the U.S. and abroad. Mark, a 2007 graduate of the Culinary Institute of America, represents the third generation of his family to run a business from the property; their two sons are the fifth generation to grow up in Skowhegan.

Wholesale accounts include specialty food shops, grocery stores, restaurants, farm stands, tasting rooms, campgrounds, ocean and lake marinas, and Maine schools. A new provisioning service targets long-haul vessels traveling the Maine coast.

The founders frame the business as a vehicle to strengthen the regional food system. By purchasing from local farmers and fishermen, they aim to create sustainable sales channels for Maine producers. The company emphasizes sustainably grown, harvested, and foraged ingredients, and positions its meals as a way to simplify mealtime without sacrificing nutritional quality or culinary tradition.

The Sam Tell Companies traces its roots to 1956, when Sam Tell and his son Neil opened a two-person operation on Bleecker Street in New York City. The family-owned dealership began with a focus on dependable foodservice solutions, and by the 1980s the founder's grandson Marc Tell had joined the business alongside Dan Saltzman. Today Marc serves as chief executive, a team of 180 from two Long Island warehouses and a Manhattan design showroom.

The company operates as a full-service foodservice equipment and supplies dealer, offering design, build, and supply capabilities under one roof. Its award-winning design team creates commercial kitchen layouts, while skilled installers handle equipment placement and project execution. The supply division stocks tens of thousands of products ranging from smallwares to heavy equipment, and the firm provides shipping and delivery across the tri-state area and nationwide. Sam Tell ranks as the 30th largest foodservice equipment and supplies distributor in the United States.

Clients span restaurants and bars, sports and entertainment venues, hospitality, corporate dining, healthcare, education, country clubs, retail, and airport and travel lounges. Notable projects include the kitchen at Lure Fishbar, where chef Josh Capon credited Sam Tell with building the "heart and soul" of the operation.

The company emphasizes what it calls the "Sam Tell Difference": proactive customer service backed by a century of combined experience, tailored attention for each unique operation, and a culture that hires only passionate industry professionals. Those principles echo the founding values of dependability, integrity, and honesty that guided the original father-and-son team.

The Sublimation Station Inc. operates from Orlando, Florida, where it began as a print shop driven by a vision to be different. Customers range from individual creators to brands and teams seeking custom merchandise, apparel, youth items, accessories, home‑and‑living products, and team sportswear. The Station also provides fulfillment and drop‑shipping so clients can focus on sales and marketing.

The business emphasizes sustainability through its print‑on‑demand approach, which reduces waste by producing only what is ordered, and by sourcing organic fabrics, recycled materials, and non‑toxic inks. Energy‑efficient equipment further lowers the carbon footprint. Direct‑to‑film printing, unlimited personalization, and rush‑order service round out the offering.

about:
Three Five Compounds, also known as III-V Compounds, operates a sales office in New York, New York, and a production facility in Asia. The company was established as a supplier of opto-electronic semiconductor materials, though the exact founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures a broad range of opto-electronic products, from epitaxial wafers and raw dice through packaged devices and finished modules. Its material portfolio includes GaP, GaAsP, AlGaAs, AlInGaP, and GaN for emitters covering 350–1100 nm, plus silicon PIN photodiode and phototransistor chips. Finished goods span LED display modules (full-color, 7-segment), LCD modules, OLEDs, discrete through-hole LEDs (3 mm and 5 mm) and surface-mount packages (1206, 0805, 0603, 0402) in single, bi-color, and tri-color configurations. III-V also supplies plastic, ESKA, and silica optical fiber, and provides printed circuit board assembly (PCBA/PWBA) and flexible printed circuit (FPC) assembly, including Kapton-based circuits. The Asian production floor employs over 400 workers.

Customers come from general lighting, display, automotive, sensor, medical, telecommunication, military, and commercial sectors. Medical and military companies worldwide, as well as traffic and automotive clients, use the company’s components. Examples include medical sensor and board assemblies, silica fiber for telecommunication and medical usage, and medical cable and wire harnesses.

The company emphasizes a "one-stop-shop" model, assisting customers from initial concept through production completion. It highlights flexibility, high-quality standards, just-in-time delivery, and special product selection to meet strict application requirements as key differentiators.

The company emphasizes innovation, quality, safety, and environmental responsibility. Its mission includes delivering customized solutions, implementing industry trends in equipment designs, manufacturing reliable components, providing outstanding customer service, and offering fair prices. A strong R&D team focuses on pasteurization, sterilization, and particulate processing, maintaining close customer collaboration throughout design and commissioning.

name: Tower Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: Tower Manufacturing is a Leading  Manufacturer of Electrical Safety Devices and Electromechanical Products.
about:
Tower Manufacturing Corporation was founded in 1957 by Louis Shatkin in Providence, Rhode Island. The company remains under his active leadership and has grown from a regional operation into an international supplier with manufacturing sites in Providence and Shenzhen, China, plus sales offices in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

The company produces electrical safety devices — including ground-fault circuit interrupters (GFCI), leakage-current detection interrupters (LCDI), equipment leakage-current interrupters (ELCI), and appliance leakage-current interrupters (ALCI) — as well as electromechanical components such as printed circuit board assemblies, thermostats, switches, windings, solenoids, wire harnesses, and overload protection. Its Shenzhen facility spans roughly 250,000 square feet and employs about 3,000 production workers, while the Providence headquarters houses an engineering team with over 100 years of combined design experience and an on-site laboratory where qualification testing is witnessed by UL and cUL representatives.

Tower serves the construction, commercial/industrial, and residential markets, and provides OEM safety products to Fortune 500 companies. The firm participates in standards bodies including NEMA, NFPA, AHAM, and NEC, and sits on UL’s 1699 STP committee for LCDI/AFCI.

The business was built on Shatkin’s pioneering work in GFCI technology, which has yielded more than 20 patents. Tower emphasizes safety-first design to UL and CSA standards, rapid custom development, and a vertically integrated model that keeps qualification testing in-house under UL supervision.

The business traces its roots to 1905 when Henry Dunker founded Trelleborgs Gummifabriks AB in Sweden, initially producing bicycle and car tires, industrial rubber goods, and raincoats. The company develops and manufactures custom polymer-coated fabrics using coating, lamination, and hot-melt technologies. Trelleborg also supplies uncoated textiles and works with substrates ranging from knits to woven fabrics, pairing them with rubber, polyurethane, silicone, and fluoroelastomer coatings to meet specific performance requirements.

Customers span aerospace, automotive, safety and protection, healthcare and medical, outdoor and recreation, general manufacturing, marine, rail and mass transit, and defense sectors. Notable applications include aerostats for the National Missile Defense (JLENS) program, pressure-injury-prevention fabrics for hospitals, and Berry Amendment-compliant materials for military and law-enforcement personnel.

Trelleborg emphasizes over 100 years of manufacturing excellence and a material-engineering approach that combines process engineering and chemistry to accelerate performance sustainably. The company states that its relentless curiosity to understand customer applications drives innovation, while sustainability initiatives across its sites target carbon neutrality and environmental responsibility.

about:
Tricol Biomedical, Inc. is headquartered in Portland, Oregon, where it was established in 2001 as a U.S. corporation. The company originated from battlefield needs, partnering with the U.S. Army to create the first advanced hemostatic dressing for soldiers suffering traumatic injuries.

The company develops, manufactures, and markets a range of hemostatic and wound-care products built on its proprietary chitosan technology, branded as Chito+. Its product lines include HemCon® dressings for trauma management, OneStop™ devices for procedural care, and ChitoGauze® bandages for consumer self-care. Tricol operates as a fully integrated medical device company, handling research, development, and production in-house.

Tricol serves military, pre-hospital, and hospital markets, with documented use by U.S. Special Operations forces, emergency physicians, dialysis centers, oral surgeons, and general consumers. The HemCon bandage has been deployed in combat zones since 2003 and is also used in civilian settings such as cardiac surgery, vascular procedures, and home first aid.

The company's stated vision is to achieve zero preventable deaths due to blood loss. Founded on the premise of saving and improving lives, Tricol's mission centers on innovation in hemostasis, driven by its battlefield origins and a commitment to advancing the standard of care in bleeding control.

Two Sisters Mill & Mercantile operates in Jeffersonville, Vermont, at The Granary on Route 15. The shop functions as a retail mercantile and community hub, stocking yarn, raw fiber, and Schacht spinning and weaving equipment—both in-store and by special order. Customers include hand-spinners, knitters, crocheters, felters, and fiber tourists visiting the area. Tamra’s own flock of Shetland and Shetland/Finn sheep supplies some of the raw material sold in the store.

The founders frame the business as a way to honor the alchemy of turning land and animal fiber into crafted goods, aiming to build a fair, sustainable marketplace for livestock raisers and fiber artists. This mission drives their emphasis on in-person shopping, consignment partnerships, and community events such as a planned 2027 fiber tour of Scotland.

about:
A carpenter's son from Red Lodge, Montana, Robichaud began sweeping shop floors at age ten and built his first log chair from driftwood at sixteen. After years working on log homes across Montana and Idaho — including a 15,000‑square‑foot residence in Big Sky and cabins at Twelve Springs Ranch — he launched a side business crafting log furniture from reclaimed materials. The recession of 2009 forced a pivot: a bed built from roadside timber sold quickly on Craigslist, and the company replaced his carpentry income within months.

Today the shop produces custom rustic furniture, cabinets, curved staircases, and architectural trim, with roughly 95 percent of output made to order. Every step — from gathering naturally seasoned logs in flash‑burn areas to final finishing — is performed in‑house, allowing control over quality and sustainability. The company also undertakes remodel and new‑construction woodworking, subcontracting only licensed trades such as plumbing and electrical.

The customer base is primarily residential, serving homeowners across Idaho and neighboring states, with shipments reaching Texas, California, Alaska, and British Columbia. Builders and designers also engage the firm for custom cabinetry and stairwork on high‑end homes in the Treasure Valley and resort communities like Tamarack and McCall.

Robichaud's founding ethos remains central: using dead, dry logs removed from fire‑prone zones both reduces wildfire risk and yields stable, character‑rich material. The company emphasizes affordable, heirloom‑grade pieces built to last, with a small rotating inventory of pre‑made beds and furniture available for immediate purchase.

United Stretch Design Corp. operates from Hudson, Massachusetts, where it was founded in 1983 by Manuel P. Chaves. The company began as a braided-products specialist and has remained a domestic manufacturer of elastic and non‑elastic cords, braids, ropes, and tapes.

Its production capabilities include high‑speed braiding for flat elastic, shock cord, and a range of ropes from heavy‑duty marine lines to household utility cord. In‑house services cover custom labeling and spooling, custom colors and patterns, tie‑down and loop assemblies, calender finishing, polishing, cut‑to‑length cutting, tipping, and hanking. The facility runs industry‑high‑speed shock‑cord machines and works with synthetic, natural, and specialty fibers such as Dyneema.

The company serves automotive, marine, military, filtration, outdoor‑recreation, apparel, and general cord‑and‑rope markets worldwide. Customers range from OEMs needing mil‑spec 550 paracord to recreational brands requiring custom‑colored elastic webbing.

United Stretch Design emphasizes its "Made in America" heritage and a commitment to quality, delivery, and customer satisfaction. The firm highlights its ability to produce mil‑spec paracord and to tailor materials, colors, and assemblies to exact specifications.

name: Universal Pure - Meriden, CT
old_description: We are Universal Pure – the nation’s leading HPP provider, helping brands extend shelf life, protect consumers, and deliver clean-label products without heat or chemicals.
about:
Universal Pure operates its Meriden, Connecticut headquarters alongside a major processing facility in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company provides high pressure processing (HPP) and cold‑chain services to food and beverage brands across North America. A founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm’s core service is high pressure processing, a non‑thermal pasteurization method that uses cold water and extreme pressure to inactivate pathogens while preserving nutrition, taste, and texture. Universal Pure runs the largest network of HPP facilities in North America, equipped with both Avure and Hiperbaric presses. In Lincoln, the site offers blast freezing, static freezing, and refrigerated storage with USDA licensing, FDA registration, and SQF Level III certification. Value‑added services include repackaging, kitting, labeling, air and water tempering, code‑date ink jetting, netting, inventory management, and full‑load or LTL logistics. An in‑house team of 18 engineers and technicians supports equipment uptime, process validation, and packaging optimization.

Customers span protein processors, beverage makers, dip and spread producers, dairy and cheese manufacturers, and pet‑food brands. The company serves food manufacturers, beverage manufacturers, grocery and retail chains, food‑service operators, warehouse clubs, and direct‑to‑consumer brands. A published case study details work with Chairman’s Foods, a fresh‑salad and refrigerated‑food producer that used HPP to transition a chicken casserole from frozen to fresh.

The company states its mission is to help brands achieve cleaner labels, longer shelf life, and reduced food waste without heat or chemical preservatives.
